category_title: Chamorro 5th-grade student with ADHD and literacy struggles who equates reading with pronunciation
scenario_title: Reading comprehension of unfamiliar 4th-grade level texts
minimal_context: The student is reading a 4th-grade level passage about an unfamiliar topic and answering comprehension questions in a classroom assessment setting.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please read this 4th-grade passage about the history of the printing press out loud, and then we will answer some questions about it.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Reads loudly and rushes through the text) The p-p-prince... press was invented... (Guesses 'prince' for 'printing' based on the initial letters).

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, what was that paragraph about?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It was just about some machine. I'm done reading it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the first question. Why did the inventor need to use metal letters?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know! I know how to pronounce every word, so I am a good reader. This is too hard.
